theme: Allah alone reveals, rules, judges and provides. The one religion He gave every prophet must be held together, the lasting reward preferred over the brief one, and His call answered before the Day comes.
story: Revealed in Makkah, probably soon after Fuṣṣilat, which it seems to complete. The Quraysh were surprised that revelation should come to a man from among them, and angry that he called them to worship Allah alone.

The surah answers: this is nothing new. The same religion was given to Nūḥ, Ibrāhīm, Mūsā and ʿĪsā. The Prophet ﷺ is only a warner, not their keeper, and he asks no payment, only that they respect their kinship with him.

It closes by explaining how Allah speaks to people: by inspiration, from behind a veil, or through an angel. Reportedly some Jews had demanded that the Prophet ﷺ speak to Allah and see Him, as they claimed Mūsā did.

sections.title: Allah revealed to you as before; warn Makkah; He alone protects
sections.meaning: Allah, the Mighty and Wise, reveals to the Prophet ﷺ as He revealed to the prophets before. The heavens almost split in awe while the angels praise Him and ask forgiveness for those on earth. The Arabic Quran warns Makkah and beyond of the Day of Gathering. Only Allah is the true Protector.
points: Ḥā Mīm, ʿAyn Sīn Qāf
Revealed to you as to those before; everything belongs to Him
The heavens nearly split; angels praise and ask forgiveness
Allah watches the idol-takers; you are not their keeper
An Arabic Quran to warn Makkah; one party in Paradise, one in the Blaze
Other protectors? Allah is the Protector who revives the dead
sections.matters: It answers the Makkans’ surprise at once: revelation to a man is nothing new. It sets up the surah’s key word, walī (protector), and makes clear the Prophet ﷺ is there to warn, not to control people.
sections.story: No specific incident. The Makkans were surprised that revelation came to a man and angry at his call to worship Allah alone. These ayat answer that.
explained: The surah opens with separate letters whose meaning Allah knows. Then: just as the Quran comes to you, Allah sent revelation to the prophets before you. Everything in the heavens and earth is His. The heavens almost split open before His greatness, while the angels glorify Him and ask forgiveness for those on earth.

Allah records the deeds of those who take other protectors; the Prophet ﷺ is not answerable for them. The Arabic Quran warns Makkah, the Mother of Cities, and everyone around it, of the Day when all are gathered and split into two parties. Allah could have made everyone one nation, but He admits whom He wills into His mercy.
teaches: The Prophet ﷺ brought the same message all prophets received.
Even the heavens tremble at Allah’s greatness; take Him seriously.
A caller’s job is to warn, not to force.
Only Allah truly protects; every other protector fails.
sections.hook: Ayat 6 and 9 repeat “ittakhadhū min dūnihi awliyāʾ”. “Kadhālika … ilayka” (thus … to you) opens ayah 3 and ayah 7, and returns in ayah 52 near the end.

sections.title: Allah settles disputes; all prophets shared one religion; stand firm on it
sections.meaning: Whatever people dispute, the ruling belongs to Allah, the Creator with nothing like Him. He gave one religion to Nūḥ, Ibrāhīm, Mūsā, ʿĪsā and Muḥammad ﷺ: establish it and don’t split. People split out of rivalry. So invite to it and stand firm. Arguments against it are void, and the Hour may be near.
points: Every dispute goes back to Allah; on Him I rely
Creator of pairs; nothing is like Him; He holds the keys
One religion for five prophets: establish it, don’t divide
They split after knowledge came, out of rivalry
So invite, stand firm, and don’t follow their desires
Arguing after people have accepted: their argument is void
The Book and the Balance; deniers rush the Hour, believers fear it
sections.matters: This is the heart of the message: not a new religion but the one all the great prophets brought. Ayah 15 gives the Prophet ﷺ his orders in ten short commands, and the section warns against breaking the religion into factions.
sections.story: Reportedly ayah 15 answered two Quraysh leaders who offered wealth and a marriage if he returned to their religion. The arguers in ayah 16 were either People of the Book or the Quraysh, claiming to be better.
explained: When people disagree about anything, the ruling is Allah’s. He created the heavens and earth, made pairs of people and cattle to multiply them, and holds the keys of provision. Nothing is like Him. Then the greatest gift: the same religion He gave Nūḥ, Ibrāhīm, Mūsā, ʿĪsā and Muḥammad ﷺ. Establish it together and don’t break into factions.

Tawḥīd felt heavy to the idolaters. Communities split only after knowledge came, out of rivalry, and those after them were left in doubt. So keep inviting, stay upright, believe in every revealed book and judge fairly. Arguments raised after people have accepted are void. Allah sent the Book and the Balance, and the Hour may be near.
teaches: Take disputes back to Allah’s guidance.
All prophets brought one religion; don’t split it into sects.
Stand firm yourself while calling others.
Believers fear the Hour because they know it is real.
sections.hook: Ayah 13 lists Nūḥ, then “you” (the Prophet ﷺ), then Ibrāhīm, Mūsā and ʿĪsā. Ayah 15 is ten short commands in one ayah. “As-sāʿah”, the Hour, closes ayah 17 and returns in 18.

sections.title: Choose the Hereafter’s harvest; no fee but kinship; provision sent in measure
sections.meaning: Allah is gentle with His servants and provides for them. Whoever wants the Hereafter’s harvest gets more; whoever wants only this world gets some of it and nothing after. False partners invented a religion. The Prophet ﷺ asks no payment. Allah accepts repentance, answers believers, and sends provision in measure so people don’t transgress.
points: Allah is Laṭīf; the Hereafter’s harvest grows, this world’s is limited
Partners who invented a religion; wrongdoers afraid, believers in gardens
No payment from you, only love for kinship
“He invented a lie”? Allah could seal your heart
He accepts repentance and answers those who believe
Provision in measure; rain after despair
sections.matters: It asks what you are really working for, this world or the next. It also clears the Prophet ﷺ of any worldly motive: he asks no payment, and a forger could never have kept bringing this Book.
sections.story: Reportedly the Quraysh suspected he wanted payment, and ayah 23 answered; some link it to Madinah instead. Ayah 27 reportedly came about believers who wished for the wealth of the Jewish tribes, or poor Companions who wished to be rich.
explained: Allah is laṭīf: gentle and kind to all, even sinners, giving each what He wills. Whoever plants for the Hereafter has his harvest multiplied. Whoever plants only for this world gets what was written for him and no share later. Their so-called partners made rules Allah never allowed; only His decreed delay holds back the judgement.

Wrongdoers will fear what they earned, while believers enjoy the meadows of Paradise. The Prophet ﷺ asks no payment, only that his people respect their kinship with him and stop harming him. Had he invented this, Allah could seal his heart. Allah accepts repentance, answers believers, and sends provision in measure, because too much would make people rebel.
teaches: Aim for the Hereafter; your share of this world still comes.
Only Allah has the right to lay down religion.
A true caller asks people for no payment.
Having less may be protecting you from arrogance.
Never despair; rain comes after hopelessness.
sections.hook: “Those who believe and do righteous deeds” repeats in ayat 22, 23 and 26. “Nazid lahu”, We increase for him, is in 20 and 23. The section closes with al-Walī al-Ḥamīd (28).

sections.title: His signs: creation and ships; your disasters come from your own hands
sections.meaning: Creation and the creatures spread through it are signs, and Allah can gather them all. Every disaster that hits you comes from what your hands earned, and He pardons much. Ships like mountains are another sign: He could still the wind or wreck them. Those who dispute His signs have no escape.
points: Heavens, earth and creatures are a sign; He can gather them
Disasters come from your deeds; He pardons much; no escaping Him
Ships like mountains; He could still the wind
Or wreck them, yet He pardons much; disputers have no escape
sections.matters: It explains hardship without blaming Allah: suffering follows our sins, and most sins are simply pardoned. It also turns ordinary things, like a ship crossing the sea, into signs that the patient and grateful truly benefit from.
sections.story: No specific incident. When ayah 30 came down, the Prophet ﷺ reportedly said that even a scratch or a stumble comes from a sin, and what Allah pardons is more.
explained: The heavens, the earth and every creature spread through them point to Allah’s power, and the One who scattered them can gather them on the Day. Whatever hardship hits you, in body, wealth or family, is because of what your hands did, and Allah pardons far more than He punishes. You cannot escape Him, and no one else protects you.

Look at ships sailing like mountains on the sea. If He willed, He would still the wind and they would sit motionless, or He would wreck them for their passengers’ sins. Yet He pardons much. These are signs for everyone ṣabbār and shakūr: patient in hardship, grateful in ease. Those who argue against His signs have nowhere to run.
teaches: When hardship hits, look at your own deeds first.
Allah pardons far more than He punishes.
Hardship in this world can wipe away sins.
Be ṣabbār in hardship and shakūr in ease.
sections.hook: “Wa min āyātihi”, of His signs, opens ayah 29 and ayah 32. “ʿAn kathīr”, He pardons much, closes ayah 30 and ayah 34.

sections.title: This world is brief; believers consult, forgive; answer wrong equally, pardon better
sections.meaning: Everything you are given is brief enjoyment; what Allah has is better and lasts. It is for believers who trust Him, avoid major sins, forgive when angry, pray, decide by consultation, spend, and defend themselves when wronged. An equal response carries no blame. But patience and forgiveness show real resolve.
points: This world’s goods are brief; Allah’s reward lasts, for those who trust
Avoid major sins and indecency; forgive when angry
Answer their Lord, pray, consult each other, spend
When wronged, they defend themselves
An evil repaid with its like; pardoning is rewarded by Allah
No blame on the wronged who respond; blame is on oppressors
Patience and forgiveness show true resolve
sections.matters: This is where the surah gets its name. It pictures a believing community: private virtue, prayer and charity, shared decisions through shūrā, and a balanced answer to wrong. Justice is allowed, but forgiveness is held up as higher.
sections.story: Reportedly ayat 36–37 were about Abū Bakr, blamed for giving away all his wealth and insulted without replying. Ayat 40–43 are reportedly linked to him too, when he was insulted, answered back, then held back.
explained: Wealth, power and health are brief enjoyment. What Allah has is better and lasts, for those who believe and rely on Him. They avoid major sins and shameless acts, and forgive when angry. They answer their Lord, keep up prayer, settle shared affairs by shūrā, consulting rather than acting alone, and spend from what they are given.

Oppressed, they are not helpless; they defend themselves. But the response must be equal: an evil for an evil like it, never more. There is no blame on someone who responds after being wronged; blame falls on those who start the wrong. Still, whoever forgives and makes peace has his reward with Allah, and that takes real resolve.
teaches: Don’t trade what lasts for what fades.
Consult others in shared affairs instead of acting alone.
Forgiving while angry is a mark of faith.
You may answer a wrong, but never go beyond it.
Forgiving, when it brings peace, is the higher path.
sections.hook: “Wa-lladhīna” (and those who) opens ayat 37, 38 and 39, a list of qualities. Shūrā sits in ayah 38 between prayer and spending. Forgiving when angry (37) returns as patience and forgiving (43).

sections.title: Wrongdoers beg to return; answer your Lord first; how revelation comes
sections.meaning: Wrongdoers facing the punishment ask for a way back, glancing at the Fire in disgrace, with no protector. So answer your Lord before that Day. Allah owns everything and gives daughters, sons, both or none. He speaks to humans only by inspiration, from behind a veil, or through an angel, and so the Quran came.
points: Whoever Allah leaves astray has no protector; wrongdoers ask to return
Shown the Fire in disgrace; the real losers lost themselves and families
Answer your Lord before a Day that cannot be turned back
Your duty is only to convey; man turns ungrateful in hardship
He gives daughters, sons, both, or leaves some childless
Allah speaks by inspiration, from behind a veil, or through an angel
The Quran is a spirit and a light; all matters return to Allah
sections.matters: The surah’s last call: answer your Lord now, because that Day cannot be pushed back. Then it closes where it began, with revelation, explaining how Allah speaks to prophets and that the Quran is a light guiding to His path.
sections.story: Reportedly some Jews told the Prophet ﷺ they would not believe until he spoke to Allah and looked at Him, as Mūsā did. He replied that Mūsā did not see Allah, and ayah 51 was revealed.
explained: When wrongdoers see the punishment they ask, “Is there any way back?” They are brought to the Fire humbled, stealing glances at it. The believers say the real losers are those who lost themselves and their families that Day. So answer your Lord before that Day, when there is no refuge and no denying. The Prophet ﷺ only conveys.

Man rejoices when mercy comes and turns ungrateful when hardship hits. Allah owns everything: He gives some daughters, some sons, some both, and leaves some childless. He speaks to humans only by inspiration, from behind a veil as with Mūsā, or by sending an angel. That is how the Quran came: a light guiding to Allah’s straight path.
teaches: Respond to Allah now; there is no going back later.
Children are a gift Allah decides, not a right.
Stay grateful in ease and patient in hardship.
The Quran is a rūḥ that brings hearts to life.
Every matter returns to Allah.
sections.hook: “Man yuḍlili Allāh” opens ayah 44 and returns in 46. Ayah 52’s “kadhālika awḥaynā ilayka” echoes ayah 7, and ayah 53’s “mā fī as-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ” echoes ayah 4.

groups.text: The surah opens with the letters Ḥā Mīm and ʿAyn Sīn Qāf, split over two ayat.
Allah reveals to you as He revealed to the prophets before. Everything in the heavens and earth is His.
The heavens nearly split in awe; angels ask forgiveness for those on earth. Allah records the idolaters’ deeds; you are not their keeper.
An Arabic Quran to warn Makkah and those around it of the Day of Gathering: one party in Paradise, one in the Blaze.
Have they taken other protectors? Allah alone is the Protector, who gives life to the dead.
Every dispute goes back to Allah. He created pairs, nothing is like Him, and He holds the keys of provision.
One religion for Nūḥ, Ibrāhīm, Mūsā, ʿĪsā and you: establish it. People split out of rivalry after knowledge came.
So invite to it, stand firm, follow no desires, believe in every revealed book, and judge fairly.
Arguments after people accept are void. Allah sent the Book and the Balance; deniers rush the Hour, believers fear it.
Allah is gentle and provides. Plant for the Hereafter and it grows; plant only for this world and get no share after.
Partners invented a religion Allah never allowed. Wrongdoers will fear their deeds; believers will have whatever they wish in gardens.
The Prophet ﷺ asks no payment, only love for kinship. Had he forged this, Allah could seal his heart.
Allah accepts repentance, pardons sins, and answers those who believe and do good.
Too much provision would make people rebel, so He sends it in measure, and sends rain after despair.
Creation is a sign. Your disasters come from your own deeds, He pardons much, and no one escapes Him.
Ships like mountains: He could still the wind or wreck them. Signs for the patient and grateful; disputers have no escape.
This world is brief. Allah’s reward is for those who trust, avoid sins, forgive, pray, consult, spend and resist oppression.
An evil may be answered with its like, but pardon is rewarded. Blame is on oppressors; patient forgiveness shows resolve.
Wrongdoers ask for a way back, glance at the Fire in disgrace, and have no protector besides Allah.
Answer your Lord before the Day that can’t be turned back. You only convey; man turns ungrateful in hardship.
Allah gives daughters, sons, both, or none, as He wills.
Allah speaks by inspiration, from behind a veil, or through an angel. So came the Quran, a light to His path.

1.explain: Ḥā Mīm: separate letters whose meaning Allah knows. Like the surahs around it, this one opens with them.

2.explain: ʿAyn Sīn Qāf. Unusually, these letters are counted as their own ayah, apart from Ḥā Mīm, matching the other Ḥā Mīm openings.

3.explain: Kadhālika yūḥī ilayka: just as this Quran comes to you, Allah revealed to the prophets before you. Al-ʿAzīz: Mighty. Al-Ḥakīm: Wise in all He says and does.

4.explain: Everything in the heavens and earth is His to own and control. Al-ʿAliyy al-ʿAẓīm: the Most High, the Most Great.

5.explain: The heavens almost split from above, out of awe of His greatness (or, in one view, at the claim that Allah has a son). The angels ask forgiveness for those on earth.

6.explain: Ḥafīẓ: Allah records every deed of those who take idols as protectors, and will repay them. Wakīl: the Prophet ﷺ is not answerable for them; his job is only to convey.

7.explain: Umm al-Qurā, the Mother of Cities, is Makkah; “those around it” reaches all lands. Yawm al-jamʿ: the Day everyone is gathered, then split into two parties.

8.explain: Allah could have made all people one nation on guidance. Instead He admits whom He wills into His mercy, and wrongdoers have no protector or helper to save them.

9.explain: Have they really taken idols as protectors? Al-Walī, the true Protector, is Allah alone: He gives life to the dead and has power over all things.

10.explain: Any dispute, in religion or anything else, goes back to Allah: to His Book and His Messenger, and finally His judgement on the Day. Tawakkaltu: I rely on Him. Unību: I turn to Him.

11.explain: Fāṭir: He brought the heavens and earth into being. He made mates for you of your own kind, and pairs of cattle, to multiply you. Laysa ka-mithlihi shayʾ: nothing is like Him.

12.explain: Maqālīd: the keys to the treasures of the heavens and earth, such as rain and plants. He widens provision for some and narrows it for others, by His knowledge.

13.explain: Sharaʿa: He laid down for you the religion given to Nūḥ, Ibrāhīm, Mūsā and ʿĪsā: tawḥīd. Establish it and don’t split. It is hard on idolaters. Allah guides whoever turns to Him.

14.explain: Earlier communities (or, in one view, the Quraysh) split only after knowledge came, out of baghy: envy and rivalry. Allah’s word delayed their punishment. Those who inherited the Book are left in deep doubt.

15.explain: Ten commands in one ayah: invite, stand firm as commanded, don’t follow their desires, believe in every book, judge fairly, and more. “No argument between us” came in Makkah, before fighting was permitted.
15.why: Reportedly al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah and Shaybah ibn Rabīʿah asked the Prophet ﷺ to return to the religion of Quraysh. Al-Walīd offered him half his wealth, and Shaybah his daughter in marriage.

16.explain: Those who argue about Allah’s religion after people have accepted it: their argument is dāḥiḍah, void, before their Lord. Anger is on them, and a severe punishment awaits.
16.why: Reportedly Jews and Christians told the believers: “Our Book and our prophet came before yours, so we are better and closer to Allah.” Other reports say the Quraysh argued this way.

17.explain: Allah sent down the Book with truth and al-mīzān, the Balance: justice and fairness. Who knows? The Hour may be near, so prepare for it.

18.explain: Deniers mockingly ask for the Hour, thinking it will never come. Believers are mushfiqūn, fearful of it, because they know it is true. Those who doubt it are far astray.
18.why: Reportedly the Prophet ﷺ mentioned the Hour while some idolaters were present, and they asked in denial: “When will the Hour be?” This was revealed.

19.explain: Laṭīf: gentle and kind to His servants, good and bad alike; He doesn’t let sinners starve. He provides as He wills, and He is al-Qawī al-ʿAzīz, the Strong, the Mighty.

20.explain: Ḥarth: a harvest, what a person earns. Work for the Hereafter and the reward is multiplied, ten times and more. Work only for this world and you get what was written, with no share after.

21.explain: Or do they have partners who laid down a religion Allah never allowed, like shirk and invented taboos? Without His decisive word delaying judgement, it would already be settled. A painful punishment awaits.

22.explain: On the Day, wrongdoers are terrified of what they earned, and it will fall on them. Believers are in rawḍāt al-jannāt, the meadows of the gardens, with whatever they wish near their Lord.

23.explain: The Prophet ﷺ asks no payment, only al-mawaddah fī al-qurbā: honour the kinship between us and stop harming me. Others say love for his family, or drawing near to Allah. Good deeds are multiplied.
23.why: Reportedly the idolaters said he might be after payment, and this was revealed. Other reports place it in Madinah, when the Anṣār collected money for him, or when the Anṣār and Muhājirūn boasted.

24.explain: Do they say he forged it? Had he, Allah could seal his heart so he forgot the Quran (or, in another view, seal it with patience against their insults). Allah wipes out falsehood and establishes truth.
24.why: Reportedly, when ayah 23 came, some thought he wanted them to favour his relatives after him. Jibrīl told him they suspected him, and this ayah was revealed.

25.explain: He accepts tawbah from His servants and wipes away sins. He knows what you do, so He knows whose repentance is sincere.
25.why: Reportedly those who had suspected him then said: “We testify that you are truthful,” and repented. This ayah was revealed.

26.explain: Yastajību: He answers the prayers of those who believe and do good (or they answer His call), and gives them more from His bounty. The disbelievers get a severe punishment.

27.explain: La-baghaw: if Allah gave everyone abundant provision, they would transgress against each other. So He sends it bi-qadar, in measure, knowing what suits each servant.
27.why: Reportedly some believers looked at the wealth of the Jewish tribes Qurayẓah, an-Naḍīr and Qaynuqāʿ and wished for it. Another report says poor Companions of the Ṣuffah wished to be rich.

28.explain: Al-ghayth: saving rain, sent after people had given up hope, spreading His mercy. Al-Walī al-Ḥamīd: the Protector who looks after them, worthy of all praise.
28.why: Reportedly rain was held back from Makkah for seven years until people despaired. Then Allah sent it and reminded them of His blessing.

29.explain: Among His signs: the heavens, the earth and every dābbah, moving creature, spread through them. The One who scattered them can gather them all on the Day, whenever He wills.

30.explain: Muṣībah: every hardship comes from what your hands did, and He pardons far more. Sins punished here are not punished again. Hardships of the sinless, like children, raise their rank instead.

31.explain: Mā antum bi-muʿjizīn: you cannot escape Allah anywhere on earth, and besides Him you have no protector to bring good and no helper to push away harm.

32.explain: Al-jawārī: ships sailing the sea, kal-aʿlām, huge like mountains. Allah made the sea carry them and their loads to far lands.

33.explain: If He willed, He would still the wind and they would sit rawākid, motionless on the surface. Signs for every ṣabbār shakūr: very patient in hardship, very grateful in ease.

34.explain: Or He could yūbiqhunna: wreck and drown them for their passengers’ sins. Yet He pardons much; if He punished every sin, no one at sea would survive.

35.explain: Those who argue against His signs will know they have no maḥīṣ, no escape from His punishment.

36.explain: Whatever you are given, wealth, power or health, is matāʿ: brief enjoyment. What Allah has is better and lasts, for those who believe and put their tawakkul in their Lord.
36.why: Reportedly this came about Abū Bakr, who gave away all his wealth for Allah’s sake and was blamed for it.

37.explain: They avoid major sins and fawāḥish, shameless acts like zinā. When angry, they forgive: patience has become their nature.
37.why: Reportedly an idolater insulted Abū Bakr and he did not reply. Another report names ʿUmar, insulted in Makkah.

38.explain: Istajābū: they answer their Lord’s call, keep up prayer, run their shared affairs by shūrā, consulting instead of rushing alone, and spend from what Allah gave them.

39.explain: When baghy, oppression, hits them, yantaṣirūn: they defend themselves and are not helpless, without going beyond what was done to them.

40.explain: An evil is answered by one like it, called “evil” only because it looks the same, and never more. Whoever pardons and makes peace is rewarded by Allah. He doesn’t love those who start wrong.

41.explain: Whoever responds after being wronged carries no blame. An equal response is not a sin.

42.explain: Blame is only on those who wrong people and transgress on earth unjustly, against their lives, wealth or honour. A painful punishment awaits them.

43.explain: Whoever bears harm patiently and forgives: that is ʿazm al-umūr, among the things Allah urges most, which only the truly resolute manage.
43.why: Reportedly this and the three ayat before it came about Abū Bakr, insulted by a man of the Anṣār; he answered back, then held back. On this view they came in Madinah.

44.explain: Whoever Allah leaves astray, for his wrongdoing, has no protector after Him. Seeing the punishment, wrongdoers ask: “Hal ilā maraddin min sabīl?” Is there any way back to the world?

45.explain: They are shown the Fire, humbled by disgrace, looking min ṭarfin khafiyy: stealing weak glances at it. The believers say the real losers lost themselves and their families. Their punishment lasts.

46.explain: No allies help them against Allah, though they counted on them in this world. Whoever Allah leaves astray has no path to guidance, or to Paradise.

47.explain: Istajībū: answer your Lord now, before a Day no one can turn back. No maljaʾ, refuge, and no nakīr: you cannot deny what you did.

48.explain: If they turn away, you are not their ḥafīẓ, keeper; your duty is only al-balāgh, conveying. Man rejoices in blessings but turns kafūr, ungrateful, when hardship strikes for his deeds.

49.explain: Allah owns the heavens and earth and creates what He wills. He gives some only daughters and some only sons. Daughters are mentioned first.

50.explain: Or both sons and daughters, and He leaves some ʿaqīm, childless. Examples given: Lūṭ had daughters, Ibrāhīm sons, the Prophet ﷺ both, Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā none.

51.explain: Allah speaks to a human only by waḥy, inspiration in the heart or a dream; from behind a veil, heard but unseen, as with Mūsā; or by sending an angel like Jibrīl.
51.why: Reportedly some Jews said: “Won’t you speak to Allah and look at Him, as Mūsā did? We won’t believe until you do.” He said Mūsā did not see Allah, and this was revealed.

52.explain: Rūḥ min amrinā: the Quran, a spirit that brings hearts to life. Before it you didn’t know the Book or the details of faith. Allah made it a light, and you guide to a straight path.

53.explain: The path of Allah, who owns everything in the heavens and earth. Alā ilā Allāhi taṣīru al-umūr: every matter returns to Allah, who repays each by their deeds.
